body: If you set a small memory limit are you able you trigger the memory error without attachments?
Confirmed that it occurs without using attachments

Oh I remember this one, I was about to report that some time ago but forgot about it. Somehow the memory used for the transport instance is not being released, despite the object being destructed (at least the destructor is being invoked).

AFAIR this is unrelated to the socket, as the memory wasn't released even when no socket is being constructed, and thus no data being sent at all. If I remember correctly nulling `SmtpTransport::$_cakeEmail` (especially this one) and `SmtpTransport::$_content` on disconnect, or `Email::$_transport` on destruction fixed it.

On a side note, you can also reuse transports, wich might be a good idea for mass mailings, that way you can keep the connection alive to avoid running into possible connection-limits.

``` php
    'EmailTransport' => [
        'smtp' => [
            'className' => 'Smtp',
            // ...
            'keepAlive' => true
        ],
    ],
```

---

``` php
$config = Email::configTransport('smtp');
$transport = new SmtpTransport($config);

foreach($recipients as $recipient) {                             
    $email = new Email();
    $email
        ->transport($transport)
        ->from($from)
        ->sender($sender)
        ->to($recipient)
        ->subject($subject)
        ->emailFormat('html')
        ->attachments($attachments)
        ->replyTo($sender)
        ->send($body);
}

$transport->disconnect();
```

Thank you @ndm2, that seems to be exactly what is happening.

Switching to using a constant SmtpTransport has provided a helpful workaround, many thanks!
